doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Miles, Monk and the New York circle
title: Regretting not going to Monk
summary: Lloyd laments not going to Monk's house, calling Monk and Strayhorn the composers he most admires.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: In a way, I don't lament that. I lament the Monk finishing school.

Because had I'd gone with Monk, he's the architect that I most, he and Strayhorn. Something about those guys as composers, and as having a whirl, Monk was somebody. I was scared to death of him. I wouldn't go up to his house. You know if he had said "Hey Charles." But Monk wouldn't do any of that stuff, but I think it would've been, I still play songs to him all the time on my recordings.
